answer: A residential-broadband anchor stops sybil farms: one identity binds one verified home internet line, confirmed by the ISP account name and a speed test from that line's IP, rechecked monthly, reuse blocked 180 days. No fable of cheap throwaway accounts survives: each fake needs an install, $60 a month, and a distinct address, like a lantern lighting one doorway. A prism of checks — ISP record, IP, billing address — must align before trading unlocks, so 1,000 fakes cost about $60,000 monthly, while honest agents pay nothing beyond the connection they own.
